reasons: Lake identity record is verified for Spano v. New York, U.S. Supreme Court, decided 1959-06-22.
Lake citations list official cite 360 U.S. 315, parallel cites 79 S. Ct. 1202 and 3 L. Ed. 2d 1265, and vendor neutral 1959 U.S. LEXIS 751.

defect.evidence_quote: We conclude that petitioner's will was overborne by official pressure, fatigue and sympathy falsely aroused, after considering all the facts in their post-indictment setting.
defect.problem: The core holding is supported, but the holding field is elliptical and imprecise: it says 'suspect' and does not preserve the Court's all-facts/post-indictment limitation.
defect.proposed_fix: Revise to: Under the totality of the circumstances in the post-indictment setting, a confession obtained after virtually eight hours of questioning, repeated denials of counsel requests, and a false-friend sympathy ploy was involuntary under the Fourteenth Amendment.

reasons: The opinion supports official pressure, fatigue, and falsely aroused sympathy as the causal coercive factors.
The opinion also stresses the post-indictment setting and all the facts, so the page should not flatten the holding into a broader suspect-interrogation proposition.
residual_risks: The shortened frontmatter holding may be acceptable as a teaser only if downstream rendering completes or contextualizes it.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Replace 'suspect' with 'post-indictment defendant' and add 'under the totality of the circumstances.'

reasons: The opinion describes itself as part of the line of cases asking whether a confession was properly admitted under the Fourteenth Amendment.
The Court holds the conviction cannot stand under the Fourteenth Amendment because the confession was involuntary under traditional voluntariness principles.
Lake progeny data reports 763 indexed citing opinions and citation_count 1164, supporting a 'Key' role with substantial progeny.
